author: Good Enough
description:
Medieval eye surgery was terrifying, especially procedures like cataract couching used long before modern ophthalmology. Surgeons treated blindness and severe vision problems by inserting a sharp instrument into the eye and pushing the cloudy lens out of the line of sight.

Known as couching, this ancient eye surgery could sometimes restore limited vision, but without modern anesthesia, sterile instruments, or antibiotics, the risks of infection, permanent damage, and blindness were extremely high. Other medieval eye treatments could be just as crude and dangerous.

This Short explores medieval eye surgery, cataract couching, medieval medicine, early ophthalmology, and the frightening treatments people endured before modern eye care existed.
